Task 3: Combining Excel and Delimited Data

There is an excel version of the white wine data set available at https://www4.stat.ncsu.edu/~online/ datasets/white-wine.xlsx. • Download this file • Place it in a folder you know (such as your working directory for your project, the folder your .qmd file lives in, a data folder you’ve created in your repo, etc.) • Import the data from the first sheet using the readxl package • Print out the tibble (just call the object name)
Solution:
When you print the data set out to the console, you may notice that some of the variable names are surrounded by backticks. This is because they are non-standard (they include a space in them). We can rename them in a number of ways. We’ll do it by reading in the variable names from the 2nd sheet of the same file. 3 • Read in the data from the 2nd sheet. This should return a data frame with one column containing alternative versions of the variable names. • Grab that column and overwrite the current column names (colnames()) of your white wine tibble. Note that colnames(object) allows for ‘left hand side assignment’. That is, you can call it on the left and store an object in it to overwrite it. Similar to names(object) <- c(…)
Solution:
Lastly, add a column to this data set to indicate the wines are white. That is, add a column that has values of ‘white’ for every observation. You can do this via the $ operator or, if you know it already, the mutate() function from dplyr.

Write a basic function (call it getIQR) that takes in a vector of numbers and returns the interquartile range (75th percentile - 25th percentile). You can use the quantile function. Remove the name on the returned vector (i.e. make sure the returned item doesn’t have a name like 75% or something like that). Allow your function to pass unnamed arguments to the quantile function.
